chunks: PLL building blocks and their roles. The question: What blocks does a PLL have?
A charge-pump PLL has five blocks joined in a loop. Each has one job: compare, convert, smooth, oscillate, divide.
Knowing the role of each block lets you see what goes wrong when one of them is imperfect.
Think of tuning a guitar string against a reference note. Your ear notices the string is flat (compare). Your hand turns the peg a bit (convert and smooth).
The string changes pitch (oscillate). You then listen again. The loop filter plays the role of your steady hand: it keeps the peg from jerking.
The guitar picture breaks down at the divider: a real PLL compares against a clock divided down from its output.
Each arrow is labelled with the type of signal. The PFD is the only place where the digital (edge) domain is converted to the analog (charge/voltage) domain via the charge pump.
Locked: f vco over N equals f ref over R .
Phase-frequency detector (PFD): compares reference and feedback edges and outputs UP or DOWN pulses.
Charge pump: turns those pulses into current pushed into, or pulled from, the loop filter. Loop filter: a resistor and capacitors that smooth the current into a control voltage.
VCO: the oscillator that makes the output clock. Divide-by-N: the feedback counter that sets the multiplication ratio.
Walk one trip around the loop with a 25 megahertz reference and N equals 40 . The feedback clock is late, so the PFD makes UP pulses.
The charge pump turns them into current, and the loop filter turns that into a higher control voltage.
The VCO speeds up toward 1 gigahertz, and the divider turns it back into a clock near 25 megahertz. That is the whole idea.
"A charge-pump PLL has a reference oscillator, a phase-frequency detector, a charge pump, a loop filter, a VCO, and a divide-by-N feedback divider.

The PFD turns the timing error between reference and divided VCO into UP/DOWN pulses, the charge pump turns those into current, the loop filter integrates it into a control voltage, the VCO converts that to frequency, and the divider feeds it back.
Fractional-N adds a sigma-delta modulator on the divider, and there's usually an output divider and a lock detector."
